questions.question: Describe how the core is checked and prepared and how the coil is wound, including the number of turns, direction, layers, end preparation and what is recorded.
questions.expected_answer: The core must be soft iron or mild steel: it is held to a permanent magnet for ten seconds and must not pick up a clip on its own afterwards, otherwise it is hardened steel and is swapped. One turn of tape over the head and point stops sharp edges cutting the insulation. With 150 millimetres of free wire held along the nail, tight turns are wound from head toward point all in the same direction, counted in tens; fifty make a first layer and a second layer is wound back toward the head in the same direction of rotation to reach 100 turns, then taped in two places. Ten millimetres of insulation is stripped from each end with sandpaper or a knife on the mat, blade away from the hand, until bright copper shows. Core material and length, wire type, number of turns, date and team are recorded in the results table and the coil is labelled.

questions.question: Explain how the circuit is built from the diagram, how a dead circuit is fault-found, how the parallel bulb option is wired, and the safety rules followed while wiring and testing.
questions.expected_answer: The components are laid out in the positions of the diagram, cell holder, push switch, coil and bulb holder, and connected into one series loop with bare ends gripped by clips or terminals, the switch connected last so nothing is live beforehand; pressing the switch should light the bulb, proving current flows through the coil too. If dark, the loop is checked in order: cell orientation and contact, bare ends not insulation in the clips, bulb screwed down, switch contact tested by bridging it, since one break anywhere stops the whole series loop. For a parallel bulb its terminals are joined across the coil's two ends with the switch between the cell and the pair so it controls both; whatever is built must match the diagram, and any bench change is written into the folder with a dated note. Safety: never connect the coil directly across a cell without a switch, press for no more than ten seconds and feel the coil between tests, keep cells away from loose metal, and use the knife only on the mat with the blade away from the body.

questions.question: Describe how the electromagnet is tested against its specification, how a weak or non-releasing magnet is improved, and how the result is recorded and the magnet prepared for the crane.
questions.expected_answer: With the switch pressed the nail point is lowered into the clips and lifted, the clips counted, the switch released and any still hanging after one second counted; the specification requires at least ten clips or a 20 gram washer lifted on one cell and none retained. The test is repeated three times and averaged. If weak, one variable is changed at a time and retested: more turns, a second cell with a temperature check, confirming all layers run one way, looking for bare patches shorting turns, or moving a series bulb to parallel with the diagram amended. If clips stay hanging, the core is too hard and is swapped for a softer nail. The final result is recorded as the specification is worded, clips lifted average, washer yes or no, release within one second yes or no, cells and turns, with a one-line verdict and the next change if it fails. A string loop is tied round the coil near the head and the leads taped along the string for 100 millimetres.
